prompt: Mid-case: A gym chain wants to grow revenue. You've found that membership is flat at 50,000, but revenue per member rose 8% thanks to personal training. You haven't looked at new locations. Which is the best summary?

options.text: So far: membership grew 8% while personal training was flat. Next I'd look at new locations.
options.feedback: This claims findings the analysis hasn't shown. Summarize only what you've established.

options.text: We've looked at membership and revenue per member. We still need to look at new locations, and next I'd evaluate opening new locations. The main finding so far is that membership is flat at 50,000, so all growth so far has come from personal training, which raised revenue per member 8%.
options.feedback: The answer comes last. Lead with the recommendation, then support it.

options.text: So far: membership is flat at 50,000, so all growth so far has come from personal training, which raised revenue per member 8%. We haven't yet looked at new locations, so next I'd evaluate opening new locations.
options.feedback: Right. It states what is known, with numbers, then what is still open and what comes next.

options.text: So far: revenue per member is up a bit. Next I'd evaluate opening new locations.
options.feedback: It gives an answer but none of the numbers from the fact sheet to back it.

explanation: Membership is flat at 50,000, so all growth so far has come from personal training, which raised revenue per member 8%. A good mid-case summary states what is known with numbers and what comes next, without claiming findings that haven't been tested.

irrelevant_facts: The chain's gyms are open 24 hours.
